data.title: Correction to U.S. Appeals Court Upholds Pentagon Labeling Anthropic a Security Risk Article — WSJ
data.description:
By Amrith Ramkumar and Heather Somerville

WASHINGTON-A federal appeals court upheld the Defense Department's decision to designate Anthropic a security risk, giving the Trump administration a win in its complicated feud with one of the nation's top artificial-intelligence developers.

The federal appeals court in Washington said in a 2-1 decision Friday that the law giving the Pentagon the authority to deem a company a supply-chain risk gave Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth the latitude to take the action against Anthropic because the company's refusal to have its AI tools used in mass surveillance or autonomous weapons could undermine military operations.

"The Department had ample support for its conclusion that the continued integration of Claude into the Department's information systems, by the Department or its contractors, presented a statutorily covered national-security risk," the court wrote. Anthropic had argued that the designation was an unprecedented attack retaliating against the company for disagreeing with the Defense Department in contract negotiations. A federal judge in California recently sided with the company in a parallel dispute covering parts of the designation under a different statute, fueling uncertainty about the future of the supply-chain risk label.

Legal analysts have said that a split between the courts could ultimately lead to the Supreme Court.

"We respectfully disagree with the court's decision. Another federal court has already held the government's parallel designation unlawful. We remain confident in our position and are considering all options, including further review," an Anthropic spokeswoman said.

The supply-chain risk is normally used on companies based in foreign adversaries like China's Huawei who pose security risks. AI analysts have said the administration's move was a self-inflicted wound in the global AI race because it could damage Anthropic, which makes some of the nation's most powerful models and has said it has lost contracts and suffered reputational harm from the move.

A win for the government could give the Pentagon more latitude to take similar actions against companies in the future, analysts have said.

The rulings are part of a delicate relationship between the Trump administration and Anthropic, which are working together on the release of new AI models while the legal fight continues. The company has vaulted ahead in the AI race by many measures and is barreling toward an initial public offering in which it is aiming for a valuation of about $2 trillion.

Pentagon officials have said the department is nearly entirely done moving away from Anthropic's models using tools from OpenAI and other competitors.

At a hearing at the federal appeals court earlier this year, the three-judge panel appeared split, with two of the judges seeming sympathetic to the administration's argument that it had the authority to use the supply-chain risk designation regardless of the guardrails Anthropic was pursuing in their negotiations.

"It's about risk, and they say, 'Well, based on what we know, we can't trust that the [AI] model may not have something embedded within it that is going to create a problem for military capabilities," said Neomi Rao, a judge appointed during the first Trump administration.

Judge Karen LeCraft Henderson, who was appointed by former President George H.W. Bush, disagreed and published a dissenting opinion Thursday. "To me this is just a spectacular overreach by the department," she said during the hearing.

Write to Amrith Ramkumar at amrith.ramkumar@wsj.com and Heather Somerville at heather.somerville@wsj.com

data.title: Some Cruise Operators Are Covertly Offering Lower Fares — Market Talk
data.description: Many cruise lines have been offering covert fares--or fares that can only be offered by phone when someone calls to book, and cannot be offered on a website--to select sellers, UBS analysts say, citing a recent conversation with a large cruise seller. The covert fares are largely being offered for last-minute European bookings, as well as upcoming trips to the Caribbean and Bahamas, the analysts say in a research note. "Covert fares are typically a sign that cruise lines don't want to disrupt bookings that are already in hand by having lower rates available in the market," the analysts say. "And interestingly, these covert fares were only being offered to the largest 5-6 sellers, not to most sellers." (connor.hart@wsj.com)

data.title: US energy firms add rigs for third week in a row, says Baker Hughes
data.description:
By Scott DiSavino

U.S. energy firms this week added rigs for a third week in a row for the first time since July, energy services firm Baker Hughes said in its closely followed report on Friday.

The total oil and gas rig count, an early indicator of future output, rose by four to 599 in the week to September 25, its highest since May 2024. (BHGUSWTT), (BHGUSOILDRLW), (BHGUSGASDRLW) (USOIRC=ECI), (USGSRC=ECI)

Baker Hughes said this week's increase puts the total rig count up 50 rigs, or 9% above this time last year.

Baker Hughes said oil rigs rose by three to 455 this week, their highest since mid-August. It said gas rigs rose by one to 135, their highest since July 2023, and other miscellaneous rigs held at nine.

The oil and gas rig count declined by 7% in 2025, 5% in 2024, and 20% in 2023 as lower U.S. oil prices prompted energy firms to focus more on boosting shareholder returns and paying down debt rather than increasing output.

Since crude prices have surged during the US-Israeli war on Iran, the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) projected that crude output will rise from a record 13.7 million barrels per day (bpd) in 2025 to 13.8 million bpd in 2026.

On the gas side, EIA projected output will jump from a record 107.6 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) in 2025 to 111.7 bcfd in 2026 as demand for the fuel rises to produce electricity for power-hungry data centers and liquefied natural gas (LNG) for export.

data.title: The Cheapest Stocks in the S&P 500: Are They a Bargain or a Trap? — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Jack Hough

Inflation is stubbornly high, but not in home broadband service. There, telecom operators are making fiberoptic inroads in a business long dominated by cable television companies. The result has been discounting: UBS reports that prices for various broadband service tiers are down 7% to 14% for fiber over the past year, and 17% to 27% for cable.

For telecom, this is a good deal. Wireless customers will hop from one carrier to another to score lower monthly bills or free phones, but they rarely change, or even think about, the main internet connection coming into their homes. By bundling the two together at a discount, telecoms can hold down churn in their wireless accounts, much the way cable has long done with broadband and pay television. For cable, however, this telecom insurgency looks like a second death. First, streaming companies came for pay TV. Now, telecoms are taking share in broadband.

The first death wasn't so painful. In late 2015, when Walt Disney disclosed that ESPN subscriptions had fallen by seven million over two years, investors made up their minds. Streaming wasn't just a way for studios to pick up extra money licensing their catalogs to Netflix and others; it was an existential threat to the cable TV bundle. Shares of networks and cable carriers tumbled for weeks. But cable had a backup plan: raise stand-alone broadband prices for customers who "cut the cord" on cable TV.

Cable TV amounts to reselling programming. After cable companies pay studios carriage fees for their cable networks, and retransmission fees for their local broadcasts, gross profit margins are left at 30% to 40%. With broadband, once the lines are installed, costs to add new customers are minimal, and gross margins can reach 70% to 90%. Cable companies faced with losing a $120 a month TV-plus-internet customer could simply raise the cost of internet service from $50 inside the bundle to $80 as a stand-alone.

The Covid-19 pandemic made fast home internet service a must, and cable companies added millions of new customers and raised prices. Share prices for Comcast and Charter Communications peaked in 2021. Telecom companies at the time were spending massive sums to build out their 5G service networks. But by 2023, with the move to 5G largely paid for, telecom spending fell and cash flow swelled. The obvious choice for putting these funds to work was laying more fiber, both for cellular backhaul, which offloads data traffic and makes networks faster, and home internet connections.

The result has been unpleasant for cable shareholders. Comcast-which spun off its cable networks and digital ventures such as Versant early this year and still has the NBC broadcast network, Peacock streaming, and Universal studios and theme parks-has lost nearly 60% in stock market value over the past five years. Charter, a cable pure play, has lost 84%.

Deep-value investors might be tempted. Charter now goes for just three times forward earnings projections, the lowest in the S&P 500, and Comcast sells for six times earnings, the sixth-lowest. But the outlook is daunting. Fiber broadband, which is generally superior to cable on speed and stability, still has only about a 22% market share, compared with 56% for cable. But fiber availability has expanded to 65% of households, and is expected to top 90% by 2030, spurring further fiber share gains.

Two lesser competitors loom, too. Fixed wireless service, whereby telecoms use spare cellular spectrum to offer home internet connections, is no match for fiber on speed but has nonetheless grabbed a quick 14% share of broadband thanks to aggressive telecom bundling. And Starlink satellite service, with a 4% share, is pricey but is cutting into cable in rural markets.

For cable, the best defense might be an upgrade path called Docsis 4.0, which allows for fiberlike speeds on existing copper wires. Since cable was built for television-a downloaded service-its upload speeds are slow. Docsis 4.0 can achieve the upload/download symmetry of fiber with speeds that are good enough for most users. To retain customers in the meantime, cable operators are offering cut-rate mobile phone service, using connections bought from Verizon and others, and bundling streaming services with broadband.

For Comcast in particular, the Versant spinoff this year was supposed to quarantine the most challenged part of the business-cable networks-and leave behind a core of healthy growers. The question now is whether its broadband business is weak enough to warrant spinning off, too. Investors might want to hold off on cable altogether. UBS says the best pick among cable and telecom companies is AT&T. It started later than Verizon in fiber broadband but has far surpassed it in availability, including through the acquisition earlier this year of the fiber business of Lumen Technologies, which provides plenty of room for bundling and growth.

Let's end with a quick word on fitness, banking, and robot revenge. Earlier this month, Barron's highlighted eight stocks that can grow without much help from artificial intelligence. Among them was a catch-the-falling-knife pick, Planet Fitness, already down more than 50% this year on disappointing sign-ups. It fell more this past week on fears that Muse, a new personal AI assistant from Meta Platforms, takes the effort out of canceling memberships that consumers had forgotten about. Another pick, Charles Schwab, is off to a weak start, too, amid concern that Muse will nudge its customers to move their low-interest deposits into something that pays better.

Wall Street is still trying to get a handle on the extent of its Muse risk. When Life Time, a chain of posh gyms, fell along with Planet Fitness, the analyst at Jefferies, who likes both stocks, pointed out that while Planet Fitness members pay as little as $10 to $15 a month, Life Time members pay $245. "Nobody forgets this bill," he wrote.

Write to Jack Hough at jack.hough@barrons.com and subscribe to his Barron's Streetwise podcast.

data.title: Minister MB Patil holds talks with Gan Siow Huang, Singapore Minister of State for Trade and Industry
data.description:
Bengaluru, Sept. 25 -- CapitaLand Investment, a global real asset manager, is keen to expand its data centre capacity in Karnataka, in addition to the 42 MW data centre it is developing at International Tech Park Bangalore in Bengaluru, with an investment of approximately Rs 2,000 crore, Karnataka Minister for Large and Medium Industries MB Patil, who is visiting Singapore to attract investments to the State, said on Friday.

In a media release following discussions with several companies, Patil said ST Telemedia Global Data Centres (STT GDC), a leading data centre platform with a significant presence in India, has expressed interest in further expanding its data centre presence in the State. STT GDC operates 34 data centres across 10 cities with more than 613 MW of IT capacity, including three facilities in Bengaluru. The company is investing approximately Rs 5,000 crore to develop a 100 MW data centre campus on KIADB land in Devanahalli, he said.

Patil said there was considerable scope for deeper Karnataka-Singapore collaboration across high-value sectors such as aerospace and defence, semiconductors, aviation MRO and other advanced industries. These opportunities were discussed with Gan Siow Huang, Minister of State for Trade and Industry, Singapore.

He said further progress in this regard would be pursued through Invest Karnataka Forum and the Singapore Enterprise Centre in Bengaluru. The Singapore Government has also been invited to participate as a partner country at the Global Investor Meet 2027 to be held next year, he added.

Patil stated that the Government of Karnataka encouraged TVS Motor Company, which already has a manufacturing presence in the State, to increase investments in manufacturing, electric mobility, advanced automotive technologies, and research and development.

Hardik Gesota, Managing Director and Head, India Private Funds, CapitaLand Investment; Rohith Bhandary, Head, Investments, CapitaLand India Trust; Ritu Mehlawat, Head of Investment, India, and Eugene Lim, Senior Investment Manager, India, of ST Telemedia Global Data Centres; and Sudarshan Venu, Chairman and Managing Director, TVS Motor Company, participated in the discussions.

Industries Department Principal Secretary Selvakumar and other officials were part of the Karnataka Government delegation.

data.title: Las Vegas looks to boost traffic with rare resort-wide sale
data.description:
Las Vegas is on the tail end of a rare citywide five-day sale that ran this week. The Vegas 5-Day sale sees resorts cut prices on rooms, dining, entertainment, and attractions as the industry looks to boost tourism amid an uneven recovery period.

The Vegas 5-Day Sale, running from September 22 through September 26, features more than 180 offers across the Strip, downtown, and surrounding resort corridors. Participating properties are advertising discounts of up to 60% on hotel stays, while other promotions include restaurant credits, show tickets, spa services, attractions, and multi-night packages.

The event is unusual because the offers are coordinated across the destination and compressed into a five-day booking window. The Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority launched the first such citywide sale in September 2025, calling it the "Fabulous 5-Day Sale." This year’s event is only its second iteration and expanded to more than 180 deals.

The gambling and entertainment city drew about 38.5M visitors in 2025, a 7.5% decline from the prior year and roughly 3.1M fewer people than in 2024. However, through July this year, visitation had edged 0.5% higher year over year, with July alone up 2.7%, suggesting a modest rebound is gearing up. International travel remains a concern as Canadian visitation, historically the city’s largest international source, remains about 30% below 2019 levels.

Sector watch: Caesars Entertainment , MGM Resorts , Boyd Gaming , Wynn Resorts , Full House Resorts , Bally's Corporation , VICI Properties , Sportradar , Genius Sports , Gaming & Leisure Properties , and Red Rock Resorts .

data.title: Bitget clarifies $388M in assets affected by security breach
data.description:
Crypto exchange Bitget released an updated incident report on Thursday’s security breach, clarifying that about $388 million in assets had been affected and not $352 million as previously reported.

In a Friday update, Bitget said it would continue to pause withdrawals following the security breach, and the company had launched a bounty program to incentivize freezing or recovering the assets. The exchange confirmed that “$387.5 million were transferred to attacker-controlled addresses” based on onchain tracing — about $35 million more than reported on Thursday.

“The revised figure reflects a more complete accounting of transfers that occurred during the incident, adding affected assets on Zcash and TRON that were not included in the initial estimate,” said Bitget. “It does not reflect further unauthorized transfers. The incident remains contained and no further unauthorized transfers are possible.”

According to Bitget, the incident included addresses on Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) networks, the XRP Ledger, Zcash and TRON. Among the assets stolen were XRP, Ether (ETH), Tether’s USDt (USDT), Zcash (ZEC), USDC, USDT0, XAUt, BNB, AVAX and TRX. The follow-up report did not address comments made by CEO Gracy Chen on Thursday speculating that a North Korean hacking group may have been behind the attack.

Even with the update on the assets transferred to hacker-controlled addresses, the Bitget security breach remains one of the largest to impact the industry. Hackers stole about $1.5 billion worth of Ether from Bybit in February 2025.

data.title: Powering Community Resilience, Bloom Energy Supports First Responders in State College during ESPN College Campus Tour
data.description:

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260925045354/en/

Before the Penn State-Wisconsin game, Bloom Energy visited the Alpha Fire Company to present a $10,000 donation to support the firefighters, first responders, and public servants who have been protecting the State College community since 1899.

Alpha Fire Company is an all-volunteer department that responds to a wide range of emergencies beyond fires, including fire prevention and traffic safety at emergencies. Protecting approximately 130,000 people across State College Borough, College Township, Ferguson Township, Patton Township, and the Penn State University campus, it is the third-largest fire department in Pennsylvania by population served.

"For more than a century, Alpha Fire Company has been a trusted presence in the State College community, serving neighbors during emergencies and helping keep people safe every day," said Natalie Sunderland, Chief Marketing Officer at Bloom Energy. "Their volunteers represent the very best of community service, and we are proud to support the firefighters and first responders whose dedication protects communities across the State College region. We also thank State Representatives Scott Conklin and Paul Takac for joining us and for their continued support of the people and organizations that strengthen community resilience."

"What makes Alpha Fire Company special is that service here creates opportunities that can change lives," said Brian Bittner, Fire Chief of Alpha Fire Company. "We have more than 100 volunteers, and close to one third are Penn State students who live and serve at the firehouse while pursuing their education. Many have been able to graduate while saving money and launching their careers, all while giving back to the community. Support from organizations like Bloom Energy helps us continue investing in our people, our equipment, and our mission to serve."

Bloom will also be onsite Saturday during the pregame tailgate where fans can take part in an interactive game and learn more about the company’s work powering essential services in communities nationwide.

data.title: SK hynix US unit considering IPO at $150B valuation: report
data.description:
SK hynix's U.S. subsidiary, Solidigm, is considering an initial public offering that would value the unit at $150B, Reuters reported.

The unit held meetings with investment banks this week to discuss their pitches, the news outlet added, citing multiple people familiar with the matter. If the unit does go public, it could raise as much as $15B in the offering, three people familiar with the matter said. The size of the deal and timing have not yet been determined, the people added.

SK hynix did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Seeking Alpha.

Solidigm is SK hynix's NAND flash memory and solid-state drive unit and is partially comprised of a 2020 acquisition that saw SK hynix purchase Intel's NAND unit.

SK hynix said earlier this month that no determination had been made about raising capital for Solidigm.

“The company hereby clarifies that, while the company's overseas subsidiary under the brand name 'Solidigm' is reviewing various measures to strengthen its competitiveness, no matters have been determined as of the date hereof,” SK hynix said in a statement. “The company will make a further disclosure either when specific details are confirmed or within three months of the date of this report.”

The prolific South Korean memory maker sold 177.9M American Depository Receipt shares priced at $149 each in July, raising $26.5B. As such, SK hynix became the the largest initial public offering ever by a foreign company in the U.S., surpassing Alibaba in 2014.

data.title: US yields extend recent run higher after more upbeat US economic data
data.description:
Key points:
  • Yields rise after durable goods data
  • Investors weigh further rate hikes
  • Oil prices ease after recent gains

By Caroline Valetkevitch

US Treasury yields rose on Friday, extending their recent run higher after more upbeat economic data reinforced growing concerns about inflation.

The 30-year US bond yield hit a fresh 22-year high, while the benchmark 10-year yield hit a fresh 19-year high.

New orders for key US manufactured capital goods increased more than expected in August and the previous month's figures were revised sharply higher, in what has been another quarter of robust growth in business spending on equipment amid an AI buildout.

That report followed an S&P Global survey earlier this week showing a pickup in business activity in September.

The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was last up 3.4 basis points at 5.196%. The yield on the 30-year bond (US30YT=RR) was last up 5.1 basis points at 5.513%.

Expectations for another interest-rate increase from the Federal Reserve rose this week following the bullish data. Traders now see a more-than-66% chance of another hike when the US central bank next meets in October, according to CME Group's FedWatch Tool.

The Fed raised rates last week for the first time since 2023 in an effort to control inflation that has steadily risen, in part due to higher fuel prices tied to the US-Israeli war on Iran.

Several Fed officials have said this week that additional interest-rate hikes may be needed to curb the growth in prices.

"The only thing that they can do is slow demand down," said John Luke Tyner, head of fixed income and portfolio manager at Aptus Capital Advisors. He warned, however, that the Fed never does it "just enough."

"You always do it too much."

Oil prices edged lower on Friday as investors weighed the possibility of a truce between the US and Iran.

A closely watched part of the U.S. Treasury yield curve measuring the gap between yields on two- and 10-year Treasury notes (US2US10=TWEB), seen as an indicator of economic expectations, was at 30.5 basis points.

The two-year (US2YT=RR) U.S. Treasury yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Fed, was down 0.6 basis points at 4.889%.

data.title: Howard Amster Takes Activist Stake at Redwood Trust, Inc. with 9.0% Stake
data.description:
Howard Amster disclosed a 9.0% stake in Redwood Trust, Inc., reporting beneficial ownership of 11,269,634 shares. He filed a Schedule 13D on Sep. 25, 2026 after a series of open‑market purchases from July through September. The size of the stake gives Amster room to press for strategic and governance changes at the mortgage REIT.

Investor Intent

Amster bought the shares for investment, but he leaves the door open to a more active role. He says he may "engag[e] in communications with management and the Board of Directors" and consider "making recommendations or proposals... including board structure" as he reviews Redwood Trust’s performance.

He may buy more shares, sell some or all of his position, or use hedging tools, and he could discuss potential business combinations or asset moves with other shareholders. He has not struck any agreement for a board seat or transaction, but he signals he will act if he sees ways to improve Redwood Trust’s financial and operational results.

Investor's Background

Howard Amster is a United States investor who oversees a network of entities and trusts, including Pleasant Lake Apartments Corp. and the Howard Amster Foundation. He serves as president of Pleasant Lake Apartments Corp., is the majority owner and a director of Horizon Group Properties Inc., and acts as trustee for multiple charitable remainder trusts. Amster is known as a value-driven investor who focuses on real estate and income-oriented securities with an opportunistic, long-term approach.

data.title: Nymex Overview: Crude Futures Fall on US-Iran Diplomacy, Supply Risks — OPIS
data.description:
Oil futures fell midday Friday amid renewed diplomatic efforts to reach a U.S.-Iran agreement over the Strait of Hormuz, while continued threats to the Middle East energy infrastructure kept supply concerns in focus.

As of 12:35 p.m. ET, November ICE Brent crude was trading $3.06 lower at $103.54, with December down $3.50 at $96.72/bbl. The November West Texas Intermediate contract was trading $2.63 lower at $91.98/bbl, with December down $2.80 at $88.10/bbl.

Refined product futures were also falling. October RBOB traded 18.5cts lower at $3.3796/gal, with November down 15.04cts at $3.1904/gal. The October ULSD contract traded 14.41cts lower at $4.5862/gal, with November down 9.66cts at $4.4314/gal.

Diplomatic efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz face obstacles. Qatar and other mediators are seeking a new round of talks in Oman as soon as next week, according to The Wall Street Journal, while Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates are urging Washington to maintain economic pressure on Iran and avoid concessions that would ease sanctions or the U.S. naval blockade.

The prospect of de-escalation is being weighed against continued threats to regional energy infrastructure. France plans to deploy soldiers, radar and defense systems to Saudi Arabia to help protect a refinery and crude-oil pipeline at the Red Sea port of Yanbu.

Near-term physical supply remains tight despite efforts to restore regional flows. Brent's front-month spread remained around $4 to $5/bbl, compared with less than $1/bbl in February, reflecting tight prompt supplies. The International Energy Agency said global observed oil inventories have fallen by 507 million bbl since the conflict began, including a 95 million-bbl draw in August.

Friday's decline follows a sharp rally Thursday, when Brent gained 3.4% and WTI rose 2.7% after Saudi Arabia reported intercepting missiles launched at the kingdom.

  • Analyst David Nierengarten said that the company is being helped by Isembyld's (apitegromab) first-in-class launch for spinal muscular atrophy and its myostatin pipeline.
  • He noted that a recent pullback in shares, likely due to a US FDA post-marketing safety commitment for Isembyld and lower-than-expected pricing, provides an attractive entry point. 
  • Nierengarten sees Isembyld US revenue of ~$5M this year, rising to $140M in 2027, $349M in 2028, and $634M in 2029. Worldwide revenue could surpass $2B by 2031.
  • He added that studies examining Isembyld in SMA patients under the age of two years old and for facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy could provide additional upside.

data.title: Microsoft Launches Copilot 'Super App' in Push to Monetize AI — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Angela Palumbo

Microsoft announced an updated Copilot app on Friday as the tech giant takes another step to monetize its artificial intelligence and compete with fellow AI labs.

The company said it's making big changes to its Copilot app. This includes introducing Office in Copilot, which allows users to ask the AI chatbot to create a document, spreadsheet, or other file right in the app. Copilot will then create a Word, Excel or PowerPoint file in real time.

Microsoft also introduced Autopilot in Copilot, which is the new name for Scout, Microsoft's AI agent. Autopilot can actively complete tasks for a user.

"Give it a name, a role and a goal, and it goes to work-watching channels, following up on threads, running recurring work and picking a project back up days later, without waiting for a prompt," Microsoft said in its press release.

Microsoft stock was up 3.6% to $515.84 on Friday.

A crucial part of Friday's announcement was changes to pricing.

Microsoft initially charged for Copilot on a per seat model, meaning it charged a certain amount per user per month. That's evolving as the AI usage becomes more advanced. Microsoft is moving to charging for its more intensive agentic offerings through both a seat and consumption model. That means businesses will also pay based on how much work the agents do.

It's important for Microsoft to show investors that it's monetizing off its AI offerings. Companies like Microsoft are spending massive amounts of money to develop the best AI, and investors want to see returns on those investments.

Microsoft also needs to prove to shareholders that it can compete with the other AI out there, like Anthropic's Claude, which is a popular option for enterprises.

"Earlier this year, the main push back from investors was Copilot lagged the capabilities of the frontier labs, weakening the Copilot narrative. MSFT has always been a fast follower, and we believe MSFT's Copilot strategy has improved materially YTD," Piper Sandler analyst Billy Fitzsimmons wrote on Friday. He rates Microsoft as Overweight with a $550 price target.

Microsoft shareholders have been waiting for this launch after CEO Satya Nadella hinted at it on the company's last earnings call in July.

"This quarter, we also introduced Autopilots, autonomous long-running agents with full enterprise compliance, including always-on personal agent powered by OpenClaw. And this quarter, we are bringing these Copilot experiences together, including code in one super app spanning both consumer and commercial experiences," Nadella said at the time.

Friday's stock move signals that shareholders view the new "super app" as a positive step forward for the company.

data.title: Wheat futures slip with Black Sea diplomacy in focus
data.description:
By Tom Polansek

Chicago Board of Trade grain futures fell on Friday under pressure from diplomatic efforts to ease war disruption to Black Sea grain exports, analysts said.

A lack of details about new agricultural deals during a US-China summit also hung over prices.

The most actively traded wheat contract fell below the $7 per bushel threshold for the first time in a month on expectations for a recovery in Black Sea shipments that have been crippled by Russia's war on Ukraine. Both countries are major global grain suppliers.

There has been "a notable increase in mediation efforts for commodity movement through the Black Sea," said Mike Castle, senior commodities economist for consultancy StoneX.

"What's worth noting about this renewed push is that the focus is on Black Sea shipping itself, not making this part of a broader peace agreement," he said.

CBOT wheat was down 7-1/2 cents at $6.99-1/2 per bushel by 11:50 a.m. CDT (1650 GMT) after setting the lowest price since August 19 at $6.83-1/2.

Attempts by Turkey to broker a Black Sea truce have fueled expectations of a possible improvement in shipping flows.

Despite market scepticism over prospects for Black Sea shipments given continued attacks, large long positions held by investors and a cautious approach by wheat importers have further removed support for prices following three-year highs in early September, according to traders.

"Even the prospect of any improvement to said flow coming to fruition may trigger nerves for managed money traders holding big speculative length," Castle said.

A two-month high for the dollar index this week has also curbed export prospects for US grains, before it eased back on Friday.

CBOT corn slipped 1/2 cent to $5.27 a bushel after touching a one-month low, while CBOT soybeans rose 1/2 cent to $13.18 a bushel in a turnaround from earlier losses.

A highly anticipated US-China summit has so far not yielded further Chinese commitments to buy US agricultural goods. But the US is expected to release details on the outcome of trade negotiations with China on Monday, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said.

data.title: Pulse of the Street: Seven weeks down, a recovery remains elusive
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 25 -- A touch of green on Friday failed to save Indian equity benchmarks from a seventh consecutive weekly decline, marking their longest losing streak since the post-pandemic rout. Selective buying in realty and consumer stocks were insufficient to break a market slide that has dragged on since mid-August.

On Friday, the Nifty 50 rose 0.34% to 23,140.50, while the Sensex gained 0.43% to 73,895.74. Despite those advances, the indices remained down 0.88% and 0.53%, respectively, for the week.

A Mint analysis shows that the Sensex's seven-week slide from 14 August to 25 September matches its losing streak during the February-April 2020 pandemic sell-off.

It surpasses the six-week declines in early 2026 amid West Asia tensions and rising crude prices, and in mid-2025, when US tariff concerns and subdued earnings weighed on sentiment. Foreign selling compounded both downturns. The index also recorded five-week losing stretches in 2022 and 2023.

Crude oil futures fell 1.4% to $105.06 a barrel on Friday as investors weighed hopes of a possible US-Iran truce against renewed risks to Saudi Arabia's oil infrastructure. Yet prices above $100 remained a headwind for oil-importing India.

"The seven-week slide looks more like a time correction than a capitulation, since weekly losses have been modest," said Rishabh Nahar, partner and fund manager at Qode Advisors.

"Crude above $100 remains the main brake, pressuring the rupee and inflation and limiting room for rate relief. Persistent FPI (foreign portfolio investor) selling and heavy primary-market supply are also weighing on rebounds. A sustained fall in oil could trigger a reversal. Next week, we will track Brent, US bond yields, FPI flows and early Q2 business updates," he added.

Realty provided the week's strongest sectoral showing, with the BSE Realty index gaining 3.4%. Consumer durables advanced 1.3%, offering another pocket of resilience amid broader weakness.

Telecommunications led the declines, falling 2.2%. Information technology (IT) followed with a decline of about 1.7%, and power lost 1.5%. Financial services, capital goods and automobile stocks also retreated.

"The recent sector divergence appears more like selective rotation than a broad-based shift, as the realty index has also remained weak and its 3.4% weekly gain looks more like a technical bounce than a confirmed trend reversal," said Puneet Singhania, director at Master Capital Services. "IT continues to face pressure, while financial stocks have been hit by the latest Irdai (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India) proposals to lower commission caps and tighten expense norms, which could affect insurance distribution income for banks and NBFCs (non-banking financial companies)."

Quarterly earnings will provide a clearer test of demand, margins and profit growth, he added.

Mayank Jain, market analyst at Share.Market by PhonePe, said the contrast reflected selective buying in businesses linked to domestic demand, while cautious global spending and foreign selling weighed on IT and financial stocks.

With earnings growth moderating, investors were becoming more selective rather than returning broadly to equities, he added.

India also lagged several major Asian markets. South Korea's Kospi gained 2.7%, Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 2.1%, and Taiwan's Taiex advanced 1.8% in the weekly snapshot.

The regional picture was not uniformly positive. China's CSI 300 declined 1.5%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 1%, while Indonesia's Jakarta Composite dropped about 3.1%.

Singhania attributed part of India's underperformance to differences in market composition. South Korea, Taiwan and Japan benefit more directly from the global artificial intelligence and semiconductor investment cycle, while Indian equities have greater exposure to services and domestic demand.

Lower relative valuations also helped draw global investors to East Asian markets. In India, elevated crude prices and moderating earnings growth weighed on sentiment, although easing geopolitical tensions and cheaper oil could support a recovery, Jain said.

Qode Advisors' Nahar said India's valuation premium remained difficult to defend without stronger earnings upgrades. The coming results season would therefore be important in determining whether that premium was justified.

Regulatory developments added another consideration for financial stocks. The board of India's markets regulator on Thursday approved the portfolio managers route for investing in mutual fund units, or PRIM, with a minimum investment of Rs.25 lakh, below the Rs.50 lakh threshold for conventional portfolio management services.

The route will allow portfolio managers to build portfolios using direct mutual fund plans, including exchange-traded funds, index funds and specialised investment funds.

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) also approved broader investment avenues for portfolio managers, including initial public offerings (IPOs) and primary debt issuances.

Separately, proposed insurance commission and expense caps raised questions about the trade-off between lower costs for insurers and weaker income for distributors.

Nahar said PRIM could broaden access to professional portfolio management and benefit wealth managers operating at scale, although revenue per client could be thinner. The insurance proposals could favour efficient insurers while putting near-term pressure on distributors' earnings, he added. The final rules will determine the extent of that impact.

data.title: Microsoft Stock Is on Pace for Its Highest Close in More Than 10 Months. Here's Why. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Kit Norton

Shares of Microsoft rose Friday and were on pace for their highest closing price in more than 10 months after the company introduced new capabilities for its artificial-intelligence assistant tool.

Microsoft stock advanced 3.2% to $513.77 on Friday and was on pace for its highest closing price since Nov. 4, 2025, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Shares of the tech giant had risen 4% this week.

Microsoft in a blog post Friday introduced new capabilities for CoPilot, its AI assistant, that will connect different tools to build, customize, and scale AI across work flows.

The company said CoPilot will now have a "Home" base where users can review meetings, chats, documents, and emails. Microsoft added that Word, Excel, and PowerPoint will also be fully integrated through "Office in CoPilot.

"From Home you can ask CoPilot to draft a launch brief, model a budget, build a deck, or pick up a file your team is already working on, and it creates or updates a real, editable document, workbook or presentation - live for your whole team, not just you," Microsoft said.

The company also is introducing a "Code" capability to CoPilot to let users build their own solutions as issues arise. In addition, Microsoft said it was adding an "Autopilot" tool, previously called "Scout," to CoPilot which will be a "persistent, proactive and personal agent that keeps working even when you're not."

Microsoft said that the "Home" and "Code" features will start rolling out in the coming weeks and that "Autopilot" is expanding to private preview at the end of the month.

"We're reimagining Microsoft Copilot to enable work as it evolves and to help expand what every individual and every organization can accomplish in the flow of human ambition," Microsoft said.

The tech company has bet big on its cloud platform, Azure and CoPilot. Microsoft's capital spending reached $41 billion in the fiscal fourth quarter and $145 billion for the fiscal year and Wall Street thinks investors should brace themselves for heavier AI spending in fiscal 2027, which started July 1.

Wall Street, too, for months has been hyping up Microsoft's ability to grow revenue through Azure and CoPilot.

The latest sign of this excitement occurred earlier this week when Stifel analyst Brad Reback upgraded Microsoft to Buy from Hold with a new price target of $575, up from $530.

Reback said in the research note that Microsoft should be able to sustain revenue growth in the mid- to upper teens with Azure and CoPilot. The analyst added that Microsoft's operating expense efficiencies are supportive of stable operating margins, while its strong cash flows should limit the company's need for outside financing.

data.title: Chase Launches Data Security Center to Help Customers Manage Connected Apps and Third-Party Data Sharing
data.description:
Today, Chase announced it has begun a phased rollout of its new Data Security Center, giving customers a clearer, simpler way to understand and manage how their financial data is shared with third-party apps. The experience is designed to make data sharing more visible and actionable, helping customers better understand where their data is being shared, make informed decisions about connected apps and maintain control over those connections over time.

The Data Security Center gives customers a central location to see which apps are connected to their Chase accounts, better understand what information is being shared and take action when they want to change or stop sharing. Customers can access the Data Security Center directly through the Chase Mobile® app, where they can review connected apps, manage permissions, adjust access duration, manage linked accounts, or unlink an app.

"Customers should be in control of their financial data, and that starts with giving them a clear view of where it's going and straightforward tools to manage it," said Melissa Feldsher, Head of Payments, Trust & Security and Open Banking at Chase. "The Data Security Center empowers customers to understand what's connected, see what information is being shared and make informed decisions about those connections over time."

The new experience is an evolution of how Chase helps customers manage third-party data sharing. While some account-linking features were already available in the Chase Mobile App, the new Data Security Center brings those capabilities together in a centralized destination with clearer information, education and management tools – giving customers a more complete view of their connected apps and data sharing.

Through the Data Security Center, customers can:

  • View apps connected to their Chase accounts

  • Review information about data sharing and connected-app activity

  • Manage app permissions

  • Adjust how long an app can access their data

  • Select which eligible accounts are linked to an app

  • Unlink connections where applicable

  • Access plain-language education and FAQs about third-party data sharing

Customers should only share data with apps they trust, review permissions regularly and use the Data Security Center to manage access.

About Chase

Chase is the U.S. consumer and commercial banking business of JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE: JPM), a leading financial services firm based in the United States of America with operations worldwide, assets of $5 trillion and $375 billion in stockholders’ equity as of June 30, 2026. Chase serves more than 87 million consumers and 7.5 million small businesses with a broad range of financial services, including personal banking, credit cards, mortgages, auto financing, investment advice, small business loans and payment processing. Customers can choose how and where they want to bank: 5,100 branches in 48 states and the District of Columbia, 14,500 ATMs, mobile, online and by phone. For more information, go to chase.com.

data.title: Correction to 3M Stock Rises on Upgrade. Why This Analyst Likes Its Transformation. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Al Root

3M stock rose Friday after catching an upgrade. It isn't an upgrade to Buy, though.

Bernstein analyst Varun Govindaraj upgraded shares to the equivalent of Hold from Sell. His price target went to $171 from $145.

3M stock rose 1.8% in midday trading to $170.45, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average were up 0.5% and 0.8%, respectively.

"We are upgrading 3M to Market Perform based on a refreshed understanding of the transformation," wrote Govindaraj. "Four factors drive our decision," including an improving economy, margin expansion opportunity, improved R&D spending, and reduced risk tied to 3M's manufacturing of so-called PFAS forever chemicals.

An improving economy is a tailwind for any business. The Institute for Supply Management Purchasing Managers' Index, or ISM PMI, has been above 50, a level that indicates growth, for several months after several years below that level.

Internally, things are improving, too.

CEO Bill Brown took over in May 2024 and has focused on operational efficiency and product innovation. Some green shoots of improvement are emerging.

Comparable sales growth is expected to be 3.5% in 2026, up from 1.5% in 2025 and 1.2% in 2024. As for profit margins, they have increased a couple of percentage points over the past two years. Analysts expect a couple more points of improvement over the next two years.

PFAS liabilities have been an overhang for years, but a roughly $12.5 billion settlement in 2023 gave investors some certainty over the size of potential payments.

Coming into Friday's trading, 3M stock was up about 5% year to date and up 9% over the past 12 months. Shares haven't done much lately, but since Brown took over 3M stock has gained about 70%, 17 percentage points better than the S&P 500.

Overall, Wall Street remains a little skeptical. Only 43% of analysts covering 3M stock rate shares Buy. The average Buy-rating ratio for S&P 500 stocks typically ranges from 55% to 60%.

At least there is one fewer call to sell the stock.

data.title: Discipline, Data & Digital Finance: Celebrating Vikas Khandelwal
data.description:
On his birthday, we celebrate Vikas Khandelwal, CFO at Reliance Retail, whose 25-year career spans finance, corporate planning and strategy across leading Indian companies

On his birthday today, we celebrate Vikas Khandelwal, Chief Financial Officer at Reliance Retail, one of India’s largest and most diversified retail conglomerates. With a career spanning 25 years, Khandelwal has built a reputation as a performance-driven finance leader with deep expertise across financial planning and analysis (FP&A), budgeting, forecasting, business partnering and strategic finance.

A Chartered Accountant from the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India and a Bachelor of Commerce graduate from the University of Rajasthan, Khandelwal’s journey has taken him across some of the most recognised names in Indian industry — Ambuja Cements, Tata Chemicals and LG Electronics India — before he joined Reliance Retail in 2022. Along the way, he has worked across cement, chemicals, consumer electronics, and consumer durables and appliances, gaining cross-sector exposure in plant accounting, management accounting, corporate planning and financial strategy.

Khandelwal’s career is marked by a steady progression through senior finance roles — from Senior Officer, Accounts at Ambuja Cements, to Team Lead, Management Accounting and Subsidy at Tata Chemicals, to nearly 14 years at LG Electronics India as Head of Corporate Planning, where he partnered closely with CXOs to drive strategic planning, profitability and performance analytics for the India business. At Reliance Retail, he has moved from Vice President, Financial Planning and Strategy to his current mandate as CFO (Own Brands), leading financial strategy for a multi-brand consumer durables and appliances business with a nationwide distribution footprint.

Across these roles, he has focused on working capital and cash flow management, cost optimisation, supply chain finance, pricing strategy, return on investment (ROI) analysis, capital expenditure (capex) evaluation and building key performance indicator (KPI)-led governance frameworks — with an emphasis on digital finance transformation and automated reporting.

Khandelwal has continued to invest in new-age capabilities alongside his core finance expertise, recently completing certifications including ‘Generative AI for Leaders’ from Vanderbilt University and ‘Finance of Mergers and Acquisitions: Valuation and Pricing’ from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

data.title: Runwal Enterprises Rs 500 Crore IPO Opens Today
data.description:
Ahead of the issue, Runwal Enterprises raises Rs 148.9 crore from anchor investors

Runwal Enterprises, a Mumbai-based real estate developer, will open its Rs 500 crore initial public offering (IPO) for subscription on 25 September, with the company looking to tap investor demand amid continued growth in its residential sales.

The IPO will remain open until 29 September and has a price band of Rs 290-305 per share. At the upper end of the band, the company will raise Rs 500 crore. Investors can bid for a minimum of 49 shares and in multiples thereafter.

Ahead of the issue, Runwal Enterprises raised Rs 148.9 crore from anchor investors. The company allotted 48.83 lakh shares to nine institutional investors at Rs 305 apiece, the upper end of the price band.

Tata Mutual Fund was the largest participant in the anchor book, acquiring 13.11 lakh shares for Rs 40 crore. Maybank Securities picked up 8.19 lakh shares for Rs 25 crore, while Authum Investment and Infrastructure was allotted 6.44 lakh shares worth Rs 19.6 crore.

Runwal Enterprises recorded consolidated sales value of Rs 2,353.5 crore in financial year 2026, up 24 per cent from Rs 1,899 crore in FY25.

The company’s total saleable area also expanded to 2.07 million square feet in FY26 from 1.62 million square feet a year earlier.

However, average selling price moderated to Rs 11,366 per square foot in FY26 from Rs 11,754 per square foot in the previous year. The increase in sales value was therefore accompanied by a significant expansion in saleable area, even as average realisations declined.

Runwal Enterprises plans to use Rs 100 crore from the fresh issue to repay or prepay borrowings at the company. Another Rs 225 crore will be invested in its wholly owned material subsidiaries, Runwal Residency and Evie Real Estate, to repay a portion of their outstanding debt.

As of July 2026, Runwal Enterprises had standalone borrowings of Rs 431.4 crore. Runwal Residency and Evie Real Estate had outstanding borrowings of Rs 286.5 crore and Rs 356.4 crore, respectively.

The remaining proceeds will be used to fund acquisitions of future real estate projects and for general corporate purposes.

The company has positioned the IPO as a means to support its project pipeline while strengthening its balance sheet as it expands its residential development business.

ICICI Securities and Jefferies India are the merchant bankers managing the Runwal Enterprises IPO.

data.title: Orient Cables IPO Opens On 25 Sept; Raises Rs 165.6 Cr From Anchor Investors
data.description:
Orient Cables (India), a Gurugram-based manufacturer of networking and specialty cables, opened for public subscription on 25 September for its Rs 552 crore initial public offering (IPO).

The company also raised Rs 165.6 crore from anchor investors alloting 60.88 lakh shares to 14 anchor investors at Rs 272 apiece, the upper end of its Rs 258-272 price band. The IPO will remain open until 29 September.

Domestic mutual funds accounted for the bulk of the anchor allocation, with eight fund houses receiving 41.17 lakh shares. The list includes Nippon Life India, ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company, Aditya Birla Sun Life Asset Management Company, Motilal Oswal Asset Management Company, Invesco, Bandhan Mutual Fund, Sundaram Mutual Fund and Edelweiss.

Insurance companies also participated, with Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance and Edelweiss Life Insurance together acquiring 4.26 lakh shares worth Rs 11.58 crore. Other institutional investors in the anchor book included Goldman Sachs, Ashoka WhiteOak, 360 ONE WAM and Border to Coast Pensions Partnership.

Orient Cables plans to raise Rs 552 crore through the IPO, comprising a fresh issue of Rs 320 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to Rs 232 crore by the promoter Nagpal family.

The company plans to deploy Rs 91.5 crore from the fresh issue towards machinery and equipment purchases and civil works at its manufacturing facilities. A further Rs 155.5 crore will be used to repay or prepay debt, with the balance earmarked for general corporate purposes.

As of June 2026, Orient Cables had total outstanding borrowings of Rs 258.4 crore, including Rs 240.4 crore of secured fund-based facilities.

The planned debt reduction will therefore account for a significant portion of the fresh capital raised, while the proposed investment in machinery and manufacturing infrastructure is aimed at expanding its production capabilities.

In the grey market, Orient Cables shares were commanding a premium of around 42 per cent over the upper end of the IPO price band on 25 September. However, grey market premiums are unofficial and can change materially before listing.

Orient Cables manufactures networking cables, specialty power cables, optical fibre cables and wire and cable harness assemblies, catering to the broader connectivity and electrical infrastructure ecosystem.

IIFL Capital Services and JM Financial are the merchant bankers managing the IPO.

data.title: India’s Growth Story Broadens Beyond AI, Says Jefferies
data.description:
The latest GREED & fear report points to rising private capex, electrification, advanced manufacturing and energy demand as key structural themes for India

India’s structural growth story could remain resilient even as investor focus on artificial intelligence and related infrastructure evolves, according to Jefferies’ latest GREED & fear report, titled The Virtues Of Small Over Large.

The report argues that while the global AI investment cycle is generating significant spending on data centres and computing infrastructure, India’s growth drivers extend well beyond the technology theme. Private sector capital expenditure, electrification, renewable energy, advanced manufacturing and rising electricity demand are emerging as important areas of focus.

AI Investment Faces Questions Over Capacity

The report raises questions about the scale of capital expenditure planned by major US hyperscalers as AI infrastructure investment accelerates.

Jefferies notes that consensus estimates currently point to around USD 990 billion of capex by four major hyperscalers in 2027. The report questions whether such a level of spending will ultimately be required, particularly as companies explore more efficient ways of deploying AI computing capacity.

The report also cites research indicating that Anthropic server utilisation had declined 26 per cent from its January 2026 peak, while cautioning that the finding comes from third-party research and should be interpreted accordingly.

Another theme highlighted is the development of small language models (SLMs). Citing a Stanford University study, Jefferies notes that SLMs are narrowing the performance gap with large language models while requiring substantially lower energy and computing costs.

The report suggests this could encourage greater use of on-premises AI systems by companies, potentially reducing dependence on centralised cloud infrastructure for certain applications.

India’s Structural Growth Drivers

Against this backdrop, Jefferies points to several areas supporting India’s longer-term growth. A separate Jefferies report on India’s “new industrial revolution” identified six areas combining policy support and rising private sector participation: space, semiconductors, solar manufacturing, data centres, electronics and aerospace.

The report notes that government support for these sectors is visible through measures including incentive schemes, tax holidays and localisation requirements.

The growth of global capability centres is another indicator cited in the report. India added 111 greenfield GCCs in the first eight months of 2026, according to data referenced by Jefferies, with these centres expected to create around 70,000-75,000 jobs.

Office demand has also strengthened, with net absorption rising from 21 million sq ft in 2021 to 61 million sq ft in 2025 and an estimated 60 million sq ft in 2026.

Electrification Emerges As A Key Theme

Energy and electrification are highlighted as another major structural opportunity for India.

Jefferies points to the expansion of renewable energy, particularly solar power, and the development of battery storage as important components of the country’s future electricity infrastructure.

The report draws comparisons with China, where the expansion of the electricity grid and improvements in battery storage have helped bring down the cost of solar power. It suggests that similar developments in India could support the country’s manufacturing ambitions by reducing the cost of electricity over time.

The report also cites projections from Hitachi Energy India that total final energy demand could increase by 50 per cent and electricity demand by 100 per cent by 2035, reaching 3,365 TWh.

As a result, electricity’s share of total final energy demand is projected to rise from 19 per cent in 2023 to 25 per cent in 2035, supported by growth in renewables, energy storage and smart demand management.

Private Capex Shows Signs Of Recovery

The report also highlights signs of a long-awaited recovery in private sector capital expenditure in India.

India’s annualised nominal gross fixed capital formation-to-GDP ratio increased from a recent low of 31.4 per cent in the four quarters to December to 32.4 per cent in the four quarters to June.

At the same time, machinery imports have increased substantially, rising from USD 29 billion in FY21 to USD 62 billion in FY26 and USD 66 billion in the 12 months to August 2026.

Jefferies also notes that India is already a major global producer across several traditional manufacturing categories, including crude steel, cement, ammonia, mobile phones and solar modules, although production remains significantly below China’s levels in several of these industries.

The report therefore places India’s manufacturing opportunity within a broader combination of domestic demand, policy support, private investment and infrastructure development.

India’s Growth Story Beyond The AI Cycle

The report’s broader message is that India’s structural growth drivers are not dependent solely on the global AI investment cycle.

While AI remains a major technology and investment theme, Jefferies highlights electrification, renewable energy, manufacturing, private capex and infrastructure as areas that could continue to shape India’s economic trajectory.

The report also makes clear that its views represent Jefferies’ research assessment and that the investment themes discussed carry risks and uncertainties. It does not constitute personalised investment advice.
